A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The title is refined in v3. The additional presentation attached to v1 was also inspected and matched against the paper, distinguishing repeated material from unique results.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety fine-tuning, representation analysis, component interventions, jailbreak evaluations, and Alpaca perplexity measurements, including additional results in its appendices and attached presentation.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds affine-map approximation measurements, aggregated token attribution, further intervention controls, and suppression diagnostics.

M1.justification: The affine-map fitting, SVD component extraction, PLRP attribution, component suppression, and iterative trigger-removal algorithm remain the same. Renaming the residual map to S and disclosing more suppression details do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use STRONG REJECT, AdvBench, OR-Bench, and Alpaca for the same safety, jailbreak, and capability assessments. The added analyses use existing data and models; Llama-3.2-3B and Ministral-8B experiments already appear in v1.

E2.justification: The main comparator sets remain, but the Llama-3.2-3B comparison drops the GPTFuzz and CodeChaeleom series shown in v1 Figure 11 from v3 Figure 11(c). The separate training/test probe comparison on v1 presentation slide 23 is also absent. The added TAP cost discussion does not constitute a newly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v3 adds protocols for held-out affine-map MSE, test-set-averaged token attribution with GPT-4o interpretations, and additional component-intervention controls. Existing dataset splits, training budgets, model configurations, and benchmark metrics remain unchanged. Newly explicit descriptions of existing evaluation procedures do not demonstrate reruns.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands validation: Appendix A tests approximation error; Table 2 aggregates token attribution beyond the handcrafted example; Figure 4 adds component controls; Figure 11 adds 3B geometry and prediction analyses; Appendices D–E examine harmfulness correlations and suppression effects. Figure 4's axis labels identify C4/C5, although its caption says C4/C3. The slide-only probe-generalization breakdown is removed.

E5.justification: Appendix E and Figure 14 newly approximate projection distributions with Gaussians and report means and standard deviations. These describe variation across activations, not uncertainty across experimental runs. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds approximation errors, aggregated token rankings, component-control outcomes, 3B rank/prediction curves, and suppression results. Table 8 newly reports jailbreak refusal of 14.4% with suppression versus 96.7% without it. The presentation's per-pattern probe scores and two 3B comparator series disappear. The retained headline attack-rate table and SSFT, DPO, and SFT+DPO score tables are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: v1's Theorem 3.2, its convergence assumption, and its Appendix A proof that every residual direction contributes positively are removed. v3 substitutes Hypothesis 3.2 about principal components containing potentially interpretable safety features. This withdraws a universal mathematical guarantee rather than merely changing notation; Corollary 3.3 remains.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: multiple orthogonal directions jointly govern safety behavior, secondary directions capture interpretable features, and manipulating triggers can bypass learned alignment. The changed formal justification is assessed under T1.

C2.justification: v3 adds the qualification that large affine-approximation errors would impede interpretation, interprets aggregated token evidence and additional controls, and discusses trigger-removal scalability relative to cited attack costs. Appendix C.2 removes the blanket statement that both DPO variants learn all jailbreaks more slowly than SSFT. The main linearity and data-complexity limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies Best-of-N BASE construction, training/test usage, harmfulness-correlation computation, and the number of directions suppressed or retained across layers. It identifies GPT-4o as the source of Table 2 interpretations. These are additional disclosures, while the code link and training hyperparameters remain unchanged. The presentation-only statement selecting tau = 0.7 is lost.

R1.justification: Section 8 adds connections to latent-space alignment work by Maiorca and Lähner–Moeller, acknowledges Wollschläger et al.'s concurrent refusal-subspace findings, and adds vision-language and reasoning references. This modestly broadens positioning without changing the central research objective. The additional published TAP reference represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: The document changes from a paper with a complete appended presentation to a paper-only structure. Section 3.1 is rewritten around a hypothesis, Appendix A becomes empirical validation, and new Appendices D–E organize suppression diagnostics. The title, terminology, and several explanations are edited, although much of the main narrative remains verbatim.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 2, 4, and 8, expands Figures 4 and 11, and introduces correlation and projection-distribution plots. It removes the propagation-network display and appended slides. The SFT+DPO plot disappears while its numerical table remains. Figures and tables are extensively rearranged; some appendix table captions now overlap their headers.

improvement.justification: v3 improves evidential support by adding held-out approximation checks, aggregated attribution, and intervention controls. Replacing the convergence theorem with a hypothesis also improves calibration: v1's proof incorrectly treats an objective-preserving removal as contradicting convergence. These gains are tempered by lost probe-comparison evidence, the retained unsupported Corollary 3.3, and new reporting inconsistencies, notably Table 4's normalization heading and Figure 4's component labels. The net improvement is useful but incomplete.
